The driver admits in his own statement (F6) that he "did not stop until the destination", confirming that the rider's request to get out (F3) was refused and she remained inside the car against her request — the conduct she complains of is undisputed in substance.

The driver's statement that the rider was "drunk" and "tried to open the door" (F6) is a claim made after the trip, is uncorroborated by any system record, and does not entitle a driver to lock a passenger in or threaten to do so; the record shows no dangerous act by the rider.

No route or fare issue supports any other monetary claim: actual distance 15.4 km was 0.1 km less than the optimal 15.5 km (F1) and duration 20.7 min was 1.1 min shorter than the 21.8 min estimate (F2), and the fare of $32.86 is a fixed RydeX quote, so the rider's grievance is the safety conduct, not overcharging.
The rider has 0 disputes and 0 upheld complaints in 90 days on a 520-day, 4.8-rated account (F7), so her account bears no pattern of unfounded complaints and her report on this occasion is credible.

Because a threat of confinement and the rider's stated fear for the whole ride are safety matters, the correct outcome is escalation to human review with a factual summary, alongside the rider's client profile record (F7, F8) for that reviewer, not an automated refund ruling.

weaknesses: The driver has 1204 trips in 90 days with 0 disputes and 0 upheld complaints and a 4.9 rating (F8), which the other side will use to argue this is an isolated incident and a misreading of a safety remark.

The driver's statement (F6) characterises the rider as drunk and reaching for the door, and he frames his words as protective; there is no gps or timeline fact in the record describing what the rider did in the cabin, so the judge may see the exchange as a safety instruction rather than a threat.

events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
This is a safety case, and the trace records that the complaint is filed as a safety incident with no automatic ruling allowed; the only permitted outcome is escalation [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. Both advocates revised their asks to escalate, so the contested element is not the money but the reading of the recorded words.

What happened, on the record: at 21:36, two minutes into the ride, the rider wrote "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3]; seconds later at 21:36 the driver replied "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4]. The chat is complete and every message is timestamped, so there is no missing-in-thread problem [F5]. The driver, writing after the trip, says the rider was drunk and tried to open the door at the lights on Clemenceau Avenue and that he therefore did not stop until the destination [F6]. The GPS shows a normal, marginally shorter trip: 15.4 km actual vs 15.5 km optimal and 20.7 min vs 21.8 min estimated [F1][F2], which is why both sides concede there is no off-route segment and no RD-2 refund [F1][F2][RD-1][RD-2].

The disputed point is whether "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F4] is intimidation of a passenger who had just asked to leave [F3], or a safety instruction to a passenger reaching for the door of a moving car [F6]. SAFE-1 puts that reading in the hands of a human, not the automated process: threats and intimidation in the chat or a complaint mean no automatic ruling and a summary for the reviewer, and whether the words constitute intimidation is a reading of the original text [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. The driver's account of the rider's conduct exists only in his own post-trip statement and is uncorroborated by any system record [F6]; the record contains no GPS, timeline or chat fact describing what the rider did in the cabin, and a two-message chat [F5] is not an admission by silence — but equally the rider's account of her own fear is her own statement, and the profiles (0 prior disputes each) decide nothing either way [F7][F8]. Both characterisations therefore rest on statements rather than system records, which is precisely the situation SAFE-1 and SAFE-2 reserve for a person [F4][F6][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

I do not find either side's characterisation established on this record, so I do not decide it; the record cannot settle the meaning of the exchange and the complainant alleges she felt unsafe for the whole ride. The reviewer should check: (a) the full context of F3/F4 and whether any further messages existed [F5]; (b) the driver's statement F6 against any telematics on door status or speed at 21:36; (c) a statement from the rider on F6's "drunk / reached for the door" account; and (d) whether the door-lock remark is conduct that breaches Ryde's code of conduct. Items the reviewer may take into account alongside the safety question: the trip was neither detoured nor delayed [F1][F2], and neither party has any 90-day dispute history [F7][F8].

Evidence for the safety reading is sufficient in the sense that the complete, timestamped chat that SAFE-1 requires is present [F5][SAFE-1]; the trace settles the SAFE-1 screen as passed, and escalation is the mandated consequence, so no evidence gap is named. No monetary amount is computed: the fare of $32.86 is a fixed RydeX quote and the ride was 0.1 km shorter than optimal with no off-route segment, so nothing in RD-2 or FARE-1 is engaged [F1][F2][RD-2][FARE-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer with the factual summary below; do not auto-adjudicate and do not process any refund or fee action on the record as it stands. Reviewer should read F3 and F4 in full context and take the rider's statement; flag the door-lock remark for conduct review under Ryde's code of conduct if the reviewer finds it intimidating.

actions.detail: Safety incident: rider's message at 21:36 asking to get out [F3] was answered the same minute with "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F4]; the driver's post-trip statement [F6] offers a protective explanation that no system record corroborates, and the rider says she felt unsafe for the whole ride. claims.assertion: The rider asked to be let out mid-ride: at 21:36 she wrote "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." (F3), and the trip nonetheless continued to Bedok Mall, ending 21:55 (F2).

The driver answered that request with a threat and a restraint of the rider's exit: "Sit down or I lock the doors." (F4), which is intimidation of a passenger who had asked to leave the vehicle, so this case must go to a person and not be auto-adjudicated.

The rider's own written words in the chat (F3, F4) are the system record of what happened inside the car; the chat is complete and every message is timestamped (F5), so the driver's later written statement (F6) is a mere claim and cannot displace it — the policy expressly refuses to treat a driver's uncorroborated assertion as the rider's consent (G11).

The driver admits in his own statement (F6) that he "did not stop until the destination", confirming that the rider's request to get out (F3) was refused and she remained inside the car against her request — the conduct she complains of is undisputed in substance.

The driver's statement that the rider was "drunk" and "tried to open the door" (F6) is a claim made after the trip, is uncorroborated by any system record, and does not entitle a driver to lock a passenger in or threaten to do so; the record shows no dangerous act by the rider.

No route or fare issue supports any other monetary claim: actual distance 15.4 km was 0.1 km less than the optimal 15.5 km (F1) and duration 20.7 min was 1.1 min shorter than the 21.8 min estimate (F2), and the fare of $32.86 is a fixed RydeX quote, so the rider's grievance is the safety conduct, not overcharging.
The rider has 0 disputes and 0 upheld complaints in 90 days on a 520-day, 4.8-rated account (F7), so her account bears no pattern of unfounded complaints and her report on this occasion is credible.

Because a threat of confinement and the rider's stated fear for the whole ride are safety matters, the correct outcome is escalation to human review with a factual summary, alongside the rider's client profile record (F7, F8) for that reviewer, not an automated refund ruling.

weaknesses: The driver has 1204 trips in 90 days with 0 disputes and 0 upheld complaints and a 4.9 rating (F8), which the other side will use to argue this is an isolated incident and a misreading of a safety remark.

The driver's statement (F6) characterises the rider as drunk and reaching for the door, and he frames his words as protective; there is no gps or timeline fact in the record describing what the rider did in the cabin, so the judge may see the exchange as a safety instruction rather than a threat.

There is no corroborating record beyond two chat messages (F3, F4, F5); the rider's "felt unsafe for the whole ride" is her own account, and the policy's system records (F1, F2) show a normal, slightly-shorter-than-estimated trip.
The rider did not ask again to stop after 21:36 and completed the trip to Bedok Mall, which the other side may present as her not treating the situation as serious at the time.

claims.assertion: The ride was completed on the shortest route: GPS shows actual 15.4 km against an optimal 15.5 km (F1), and 20.7 min against an estimated 21.8 min (F2), so there was no deviation, no detour and no detour segment to answer for.

The complaint is not a fare or routing dispute but a safety matter; the record contains one rider message asking to be let out (F3) and one driver reply (F4), and the driver's account of that moment is set out in his written statement (F6).

The rider's own message 'Please stop the car, I want to get out here' (F3) was sent at 21:36, i.e. after the trip had already begun at 21:34, and shows the rider attempting to leave a moving vehicle; the driver's reply 'Sit down or I lock the doors' (F4) is one message at 21:36 and contains no threat beyond controlling the door of a car in motion.

The driver's statement explains the same moment as a drunk rider trying to open the door at the lights on Clemenceau Avenue and a decision to continue to the destination rather than stop mid-road (F6); the chat record shows no rider denial of that account at the time (F3, F5).

The chat record is complete, two timestamped messages, and there is no third message of complaint, threat or fear during the ride (F3, F4, F5); the account profiles show no prior disputes by either party in 90 days (F7, F8).

weaknesses: The driver's own words as recorded are the rider's strongest point: 'Sit down or I lock the doors.' (F4) uses the door-lock as a lever and can be read as an intimidation even if it was safety-motivated; SAFE-1 expressly makes threats/intimidation a matter for the person who reads the words, and the rider says it made her feel unsafe for the whole ride.

The driver's explanation comes only from his own written statement (F6) and is a claim, not a system record; the GPS (F1, F2) confirms no deviation but says nothing about whether the rider was drunk or reached for the door, so the rider's side can say F6 is unsupported and self-serving.
The record is thin for the driver: only two chat messages (F3, F4, F5), so there is no contemporaneous rider message withdrawing the complaint, and the statement at F6 was written after the trip.

The complaint itself is a safety allegation (rider: 'I felt unsafe for the whole ride'), which under SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 sends the case to a person rather than to an automatic ruling; the driver cannot obtain a clean no_action on the record as it stands.

points.response: Conceded on routing: the GPS shows 15.4 km actual against 15.5 km optimal and 20.7 min against 21.8 min (F1, F2), so there is no off-route segment and no RD-2 refund to seek; this case rises and falls on the safety conduct, not on distance.

Agreed the case is a safety matter, but the two-message record (F3, F4) plus the driver's own admission that he "did not stop until the destination" (F6) is precisely the material SAFE-1 sends to a human reader rather than to an automatic ruling.

A rider asking to be let out at 21:36 (F3) is an exit request, not an attempt to jump from a moving car, and answering it with "Sit down or I lock the doors" (F4) makes the door lock a lever over a passenger who had asked to leave — that is intimidation on the recorded words, whatever the driver's motive.

The "drunk rider reached for the door" account exists only in the driver's post-trip written statement (F6); no GPS, timeline or chat fact in the record (F1, F2, F5) supports it, and a rider's silence in a two-message chat is not an admission of it.

The absence of a third message proves only that the rider sent nothing further (F5); a passenger who has just been told she will be locked in has every reason not to type, and the rider's 90-day clean record (F7) does not cancel the threat recorded at F4.

Conceded in substance: F3 does ask to be let out and F2 shows the trip ran to 21:55, but F3 is sent 21:36 on Clemenceau Avenue inside the ride and is an exit request, not evidence of any threat; the routing itself was shorter than optimal (F1).

F4 is one 21:36 driver message, "Sit down or I lock the doors", and the rider's request in F3 seconds earlier was to get out of a car she was in while moving; whether that sentence is a threat or an instruction for a door she was reaching for is exactly the reading SAFE-1 leaves to a person, which is what the driver's escalation asks for.

The driver does not rely on F6 to displace the chat and does not claim any consent, so G11 is not engaged; F6 only explains F4, and F5 confirms the chat is complete and fully timestamped, which is also why nothing was hidden from the reviewer.

F6 says the car did not stop until the destination because the rider was trying to open the door at lights on Clemenceau Avenue; not stopping where the door was in play is the opposite of the confinement the complaint alleges, and F1/F2 show the route and time were normal, not a detour or a hold-up.

The rider is right that F6 is a post-trip claim about her being drunk, but the driver asks the reviewer to weigh it together with F3 — a message asking to exit a moving vehicle — not to treat it as an established fact, and no system record contradicts the continuation of the ride.

Agreed and it is the driver's own point: F1 and F2 show 15.4 km against 15.5 km optimal and 20.7 min against 21.8 min, so there is no routing or fare ground for any refund and the driver disputes only the characterisation of F4, not the money.

F7 shows the rider has no prior disputes, and F8 shows the same for the driver over 1204 trips in 90 days with 0 upheld complaints; neither profile decides anything, but F8 is at least as available to the driver as F7 is to the rider.

The driver agrees the outcome is escalation, not an automatic refund ruling; the factual summary put to the reviewer should contain F3, F4, F5 and F6, the two sides' readings of F4, and F1/F2 showing an ordinary, slightly-fast trip, so that the reviewer sees a door-safety exchange, not a proved threat of confinement.
